To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Latvian public higher education institutions have made significant progress in the digital environment and are ready to offer students and other stakeholders a wide range of digital services, but the digital gap between Latvia and the most developed European Union countries still remains.

the COVID 19 crisis has accelerated the digital transformation of the European Union higher educational institutions, which is a positive trend that will contribute to the competitiveness of the higher education institutions of the European Union.

the digital environment of Latvia University of Life Sciences is competitive in the EU higher education market, and the digital environment of the EU higher education system is competitive in the international market.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the digital readiness of the European Union higher educational institutions, the digital readiness of Latvia University of life Sciences and Technologies and the impact of COVID 19 pandemic on the digital readiness of higher educational institutions in Latvia.
the digital transformation and digitalisation processes in the European Union higher educational system and its adaptiveness to global pandemic crisis.
the need for digital readiness of the EU higher education institutions, which has become an important factor of competitiveness in the modern world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Latvian public higher education institutions have a high level of digital readiness, which is reflected by the high level of the digital environment, the availability of the digital content and the high level of digital skills of both academic staff and students.

the COVID 19 crisis has had a positive effect on the digital readiness and competitiveness of the European Union higher institutions, but the situation in Latvia has not changed much and there are still significant challenges to overcome.
the European Union has made significant progress in improving the digital skills of its population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Latvia is ready for digitalization of the education system and the COVID 19 crisis has not had a significant impact on its development.
Latvia University of Life Science and Technologies has achieved the necessary level of digitalization and is ready for the new challenges in the future.

the digital readiness of Latvian higher educational institutions has increased significantly during the COVID 19 crisis and has reached a level of competitiveness that allows the Latvian higher school to compete with the most technologically advanced universities in the European Union.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the COVID 19 crisis has revealed the digital readiness of higher education institutions and has also shown the importance of digital skills for the future development and competitiveness of the European Union higher educational institutions.

the COVID 19 global pandemic has not only revealed the digital readiness and competitiveness of the European Union higher educational institutions but also has created a new reality that has forced the European Union higher schools to adapt to the new situation and offer the students the most appropriate distance learning opportunities.
the COVID 19 Pandemics impact has accelerated digital transformation of the Latvian higher educational institutions.
